critical_bugs: Unhandled KeyError/TypeError: Direct dictionary access (obj['class'], obj['center']) on YOLO JSON data lacks defensive checks. Malformed or missing keys will crash the fusion pipeline during runtime.

Unsafe Deserialization (Security): pickle.load() is used to deserialize slam_data.pkl. Pickle execution of arbitrary code during deserialization poses a critical security risk if files are tampered with, corrupted, or sourced from untrusted pipelines.
warnings: Hardcoded absolute Windows path (ROOT) breaks portability and will fail on standard Linux/ROS2 environments used for MiR100 deployment.
Implicit camera resolution assumption: Hardcoded 2048x1088 normalization factors may cause spatial projection drift if actual camera feeds differ, with no validation or error logging.
recommendations: Replace pickle serialization with JSON, msgpack, or HDF5 for map metadata to eliminate arbitrary code execution risks.
Implement defensive JSON parsing using .get() methods and explicit key validation before accessing nested YOLO detection structures.
Externalize configuration (ROOT path, camera resolutions, clustering thresholds) into a YAML/JSON config file or ROS parameters for production deployment.

critical_bugs: Non-numeric center coordinates (cx, cy) in YOLO data cause TypeError during division in map_pixels_to_slam
warnings: Hardcoded camera resolution (2048x1088) may not match actual camera if used with different cameras
Class filtering is case-sensitive; might miss objects like 'TV' instead of 'tv'
recommendations: Validate cx/cy are numeric before division in map_pixels_to_slam (e.g., try/except or type check)
Make camera resolution configurable via metadata instead of hardcoded values
Normalize class names to lowercase for case-insensitive filtering
